A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and your traffic travels through it instead of out in the open.

Without one, websites see your home or office address, and whoever runs the Wi-Fi can see which sites you visit. With one, your device scrambles everything before it leaves, sends it to the VPN company's computer, and that computer passes it on to the website. The site sees the VPN's address, not yours, and the Wi-Fi owner sees only scrambled data.

It helps on public Wi-Fi and hides your location from sites. It does not make you anonymous, because the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
